assertions: He will not obtain the desired parsonage/benefice on this suit

There is no perfection between the querent and the benefice: Jupiter, lord of the 9th and significator of the benefice, makes no aspect to the lord of the Ascendant nor to the Moon, and there is no reception between the significators
Neither the lord of the Ascendant nor the Moon is placed in the 9th house, and there is no translation or collection of light to bring the matter together
Saturn impedited in the Ascendant afflicts the querent and the question itself, showing hindrance, delay and failure rather than recovery of his former place and credit
The Moon separating from a trine and applying to an opposition of Mercury, lord of the 3rd, shows adverse news, letters, reports or interference working against the suit
Venus in the 7th house opposing the Ascendant shows an opponent or rival party standing directly against him in the matter
Pressing the suit despite advice will not succeed; he will remain without this benefice and must seek another way to live
method: Horary astrology - Lilly, Christian Astrology Book II, classical testimonies of perfection and impediment
reasoning: Benefice is signified by the 9th house and its lord Jupiter; querent by lord of Ascendant and Moon. Lilly's horary perfection requires aspect, reception, placement in the house of the matter, or translation/collection of light - all are explicitly absent here. Saturn impedited in the Ascendant infortunes the question, Moon applying to opposition of Mercury lord of 3rd adds contrary testimony, and Venus in 7th opposing Ascendant shows opposition from another party. Seven negative testimonies converge on denial, with no positive testimony to outweigh them.
summary: He will not obtain the parsonage he desires.
